title: Frontend: Color Code Game
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Color Code Game. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({colors=[red,blue,green],answer="blue"}). Render buttons[data-color=COLOR] with visible color names. Clicking one produces Correct/Incorrect in [data-testid=feedback]. A correct round locks until Reset; answer is injected and stable.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Generate target/options once per round and keep the answer fixed while the user interacts.
alternativeApproaches: Offer an accessible non-color challenge mode and define how hints affect scoring.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Correct/incorrect choice; duplicate distractor prevention; restart.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
